symptom: Docker says it cannot connect to the Docker daemon
steps: Open Docker Desktop and wait until it says Docker is running.
Open a new terminal and run 'docker info' to check the Docker engine answers.
On Linux, start the engine with 'sudo systemctl start docker'.
If it still fails, restart your computer and open Docker Desktop again.

symptom: Port is already allocated when starting a container
steps: Run 'docker ps' to see if another container is already using that port.
Stop that container with 'docker stop <container-name>'.
If no container is using it, find the program holding the port ('netstat -ano' on Windows, 'lsof -i :<port>' on Mac or Linux) and close it.
Or use a different port on your computer, for example '-p 8081:80'.

symptom: Image build fails with "COPY failed: file not found"
steps: Check the path in the COPY line is relative to the build folder, not to the folder your terminal is in.
Run 'docker build' from the folder that holds the Dockerfile, or give the right folder at the end of the command.
Make sure the file is not listed in .dockerignore.
Check the capital letters in the file name match exactly, because Linux paths are case-sensitive.

symptom: Container starts and then stops straight away
steps: Run 'docker ps -a' to see the stopped container and its exit code.
Read the error message with 'docker logs <container-name>'.
Check the start command (CMD) runs a program that keeps running, such as a web server.
Fix the error, rebuild the image and start the container again.

symptom: Docker fails with "no space left on device"
steps: Run 'docker system df' to see what is using the space.
Remove stopped containers, unused networks and old images with 'docker system prune'.
Only add '--volumes' if you are sure no volume holds data you still need.
In Docker Desktop, you can also give Docker more disk space under Settings, then Resources.
